name: maybe_Ui_Window_ResetChildrenF
summary: Class-specific window reset: detaches children until the child ring holds two, splices the embedded pane at +0x360 back in, hides the panes at +0x1C8 and +0x294, shows +0x360 and tail-calls 0x0037AA18(self, 2) to reveal the message pane.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0037B0E8..0x0037B157 shows the extra hide/hide/show broadcasts and the tail call that Ghidra cut off at its 'does not return' warning; nothing is freed. The same drain-to-N plus fixed-pane-toggle shape is used by the sibling maybe_Ui_Window_ResetChildrenE (0x0037A9A8, R3_034), so the inherited 'DestroyChildren' wording was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_CommandStack_Unwind
summary: Pops every 0xC-byte entry of the stack at self+0x11C while the depth at +0x170 is non-zero: detaches the popped node, decrements the depth, calls the entry's handler pair and finally re-shows the entry that remains (broadcast 1).
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_DataPanel_OpenFromByte (0x003143C8), which runs it while swapping data panels; the three-word entry stride, the depth at +0x170 and the per-entry handler call are visible in both C and asm. Nothing names what the entries represent, so the stack wording stays a maybe.

name: maybe_Ui_ChoiceSelectWindow_SwitchToList
summary: Choice-select window step: hides the message pane at +0xF84 and the two panes at +0x804/+0x9D8, shows the list panes +0xB4C/+0xC1C with their layout animation, then selects the entry stored in the +0xB4C list. Nothing is destroyed.
evidence: asm 0x0047A510..0x0047A5AC shows the five visibility calls and the tail Ui_List_SelectEntryById; the function is the vtable slot immediately before the confident Ui_ChoiceSelectWindow_LayoutRows (0x0047A5B0), so the owner is the choice-select window, not a generic window 'destroy' tail.

name: maybe_Menu_Slot_ResetRound
summary: Resets one slot-machine/menu slot: drains the child list to one entry, splices the group at +0xA80, hides the groups at +0x1C8/+0x390/+0x230, shows +0xA80, rebuilds the digit widget at +0xD20 from the getter 0x0064C368 and invalidates the selection index at +0x11D (0xFF).
evidence: asm 0x004A1390..0x004A141C shows the digit getter feeding Casino_Slot_SetDigitSprite (0x004ADC2C) into the +0xD20 widget and the +0x11D=0xFF selection invalidation; this supports the slot-reset reading but no caller exists, so 'round' remains unproven.

name: Ui_PaneStack_Pop
summary: Pops the top entry of a pane stack: detaches the popped pane, decrements the depth stored in entry word +0xC, runs the entry's handler pair and re-shows the new top entry; returns 1 when an entry was popped, 0 otherwise.
evidence: The named caller Ui_TalkMenuWindow_RebuildContent (0x003B0440, now 0.50) calls it as 'pop the sliding pane at +0x124', and maybe_Ui_MessagePanel_HandleConfirm / maybe_Ui_BigWindow_InitPanes use it the same way; the arbitrary class letter C in 'PopPaneRawC' is dropped.

name: maybe_Ui_SoulWindow_Subwidget_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the small soul/equipment-window sub-widget: installs vtable 0x00768D7C and releases its five resource handles (self+0x10..+0x20) through the field object manager, then returns self.
evidence: Vtable 0x00768D7C is the same one installed by maybe_Ui_SoulWindow_Subwidget_Ctor (0x003B7640, R_013), and the caller Ui_Window_ReleaseResources (0x00315BB8) invokes this as the widget's release slot; the old name mentioned neither the class nor the five handles it releases.

name: maybe_Ui_SmithMenu_DetailPanel_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the vtable-0x0076B7E0 panel: installs the vtable and releases the single handle at +0xC through the field object manager, returning self.
evidence: No new symbol, caller or string ties vtable 0x0076B7E0 to the smith menu; the only caller is Ui_Window_ReleaseResources and the body is the standard one-handle release, so the class attribution stays unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ReleaseAttached
summary: Releases the window's auxiliary object at +0x10: calls Ui_Window_ReleaseResources on it, releases it through 0x0010F6CC (ref-counted release) and clears the pointer.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithBalloon (0x0019EAA8), which passes self->f_84 - the message window's variant widget, not a shop window; the callee is the now-named Ui_Window_ReleaseResources (0x00315BB8), which pins the release shape but not the widget class.

name: Sound_AllocFileSlot
summary: Allocates a free sound-file slot: finds a clear bit in the inverted occupancy mask at f_1AA4, marks it, bumps the slot counter, calls Sound_SequencePlayer_Init on the 0x13C-byte slot record, stores the encoded handle (0x5E900000 | sequence<<8 | slot) at record+0x14 and returns it.
evidence: The occupancy-mask scan, the counter bump and the 0x5E900000 handle form are all visible; the only caller Cutscene_Close (0.62) opens the field BGM sequence player as the cutscene ends, which fits an allocator rather than a release.

name: Gfx_PostEffect_ApplySlot50
signature: void Gfx_PostEffect_ApplySlot50(void* node, u32 chain, void* cmd)
summary: When the effect object at node->f_50 exists and its +0x44 enable bit is set, appends it to the render command list through 0x0053CD1C, temporarily exposing the chain word at +4 as the command-list scratch field f_60C.
evidence: Both callers are the named UI draw routines Ui_RenderObject_Draw / Ui_RenderObject_DrawWithTexture and pass the per-slot render node at self + slot*0x414 + 0x2C; the body appends one optional effect object. The slot number is certain, the 'post effect' wording is inherited.

name: Gfx_PostEffect_ApplySlot3C
signature: void Gfx_PostEffect_ApplySlot3C(void* node, u32 chain, void* cmd)
summary: Same as 0x001F0510 for the effect object at node->f_3C: when its +0x44 enable bit is set it appends the effect through 0x0053CD1C using the f_60C scratch field.
evidence: Template copy of 0x001F0510 on the next slot (f_3C vs f_50), with the same named UI draw callers; only the slot number and the caller context are asserted.

name: Gfx_PostEffect_ApplyFourSlots
signature: void Gfx_PostEffect_ApplyFourSlots(void* node, u32 chain, void* cmd, u32 arg4)
summary: Applies up to four effect objects (f_40, f_44, f_48, f_4C) in order, each only when its +0x44 enable bit is set, through the same 0x0053CD1C append and f_60C scratch field.
evidence: Four inline copies of the 0x001F0510 body on consecutive node fields, called from the named Ui_RenderObject_Draw/Ui_RenderObject_DrawWithTexture; the ordering is visible, the individual effect names are not.

name: maybe_Game_GetFlag275A4
summary: Returns whether the byte at GameWork+0x275A4 is non-zero. It gates the recipe-book mode sync/refresh and is also read during party-roster init; what the flag means is still unknown.
evidence: The getter uses Game_GetWork, i.e. the GameWork block whose save area starts at +0x24A98; 0x275A4 is a fixed GameWork byte, not a save-data field, so the inherited 'Save_' prefix was wrong. No caller names the flag.

name: Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots
signature: void Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots(void* self, const u8* spec, const int* ids, int count)
summary: Clears the 16 dword balloon slots at self+0x70..0xAC and refills them with the non-null unit ids; when spec[3] asks for two or more rows it first copies the ids into a 0x68-byte temporary and picks them through the battle RNG 0x001CA474(world+0x4218, 0, n-1).
evidence: The receiver is the balloon UI (the 0x001F6xxx block holds dozens of named Battle_Ui_*Balloon* routines), the callers are the named Battle_Ui_Update and Battle_ActorAction_UpdateAnchor, and the battle RNG at battleWork+0x4218 is the documented one.

name: Battle_Ui_CanSelectBalloonSlots
signature: u32 Battle_Ui_CanSelectBalloonSlots(void* self, const char* spec, void* slotList, void* units, int unitCount)
summary: Validates the current balloon selection: counts the 16 occupied slots at +0x1C and walks them, rejecting candidates whose slot/row test fails or whose unit does not report battle state 8/10; returns 1 when the request is acceptable, 0 otherwise. It never writes a selection.
evidence: It is the gate immediately before Battle_Ui_Update proceeds with the chosen slot; 0x00639954 is the battle-status test (FACTS.md), not a text-type test, and the body only returns 0/1 - so the inherited 'Select' verb was misleading.

name: Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlotsEx
signature: void Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlotsEx(void* self, const u8* spec, int first, int idsBase, int count)
summary: Same 16-slot wipe as 0x001F6D64, then filters the unit ids: a negative 'first' picks one id through the battle RNG, otherwise only entries whose virtual +0xD4 equals 'first' (or the random pick) are kept before the slots are filled.
evidence: Body is a superset of the now-confirmed Battle_Ui_ResetBalloonSlots with an extra vtable+0xD4 filter per entry; both functions are called from the named Battle_Ui_Update in the balloon-target selection branches.

name: maybe_Ui_Balloon_InterpolateAnchor
signature: void maybe_Ui_Balloon_InterpolateAnchor(void* self, int mode, int flag, u32 argument)
summary: Resolves the balloon target object through virtual +0x40, chooses an anchor source by mode (mode 0 asks virtual +0x74, modes 1/2 use the cached float pairs at +0xDC/+0x100) and interpolates the three floats into the target's +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 using the alpha in s0 (shown as in_s0).
evidence: The two callers are Battle_ActorAction_ShowRevivePopup and FieldParty_Talk_Update, both positioning a balloon over a party member; the interpolation itself is clear but the decompiler lost the s0 float argument and the member-index argument, so the wording stays cautious.

name: maybe_BattleParty_ApplyMemberStateFlags
signature: void maybe_BattleParty_ApplyMemberStateFlags(void* group, void* paramTable, void* actor, int playerLane)
summary: For a living actor, walks the 28 per-slot flags of the parameter table (+0x1A + j*2 + lane) and applies the matching behaviour: attachment show/hide at j=0/1, queue action 0x1C and register the actor in the group's 32 slots at j=6, and set states 0x29/0x15 at j=0x11/0x12.
evidence: The body calls the named Battle_QueueAction and the 32-slot group array is the same actor array used by the balloon party code; 'FieldParty' and the exact meaning of the 28 flags are inherited, not proven, so the prefix is corrected to the battle-party subsystem only.

name: maybe_FieldParty_BuildMemberIdRecord
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_BuildMemberIdRecord(void* group, u32 flags, int extra)
summary: Builds the party group's 9-word member-id record (flag word plus up to eight slot ids) from the 16 live slots at group+0x1C, clears the f_79 flag of the actors found in the four battle unit lists at +0x428C, and submits the record through the group's virtual +0x60.
evidence: The group layout (16 live slots at +0x1C, virtual +0x60) is exactly that of the named maybe_FieldParty_ApplySlotAndLayoutBalloons (0x001FC7FC), whose two callers are confident field-party/battle code; the old 'Menu_' prefix had no menu caller at all.

name: maybe_FieldParty_BuildMemberIdRecordAlt
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_BuildMemberIdRecordAlt(void* group, u32 flags, int slot)
summary: Second form of the member-id record builder: same 16-slot scan and record layout, but the per-slot id comes from group virtual +0x4C(group, slot) and the record is pushed through the global window object at 0x001FCE08.
evidence: Same group layout and callee set as 0x001FC95C, which is now tied to the field-party balloon group; still no direct caller, so the variant wording is kept.

name: maybe_Battle_IncrementUnitCounters
summary: Walks the four 0x1C-stride battle unit rings at battleWork+0x4298..+0x42EC; for every live unit (virtual +0x10 non-zero) whose flag word +0x39D has none of 0x46 set, increments the capped u32 per-unit counter at saveWork+0x3AE4+id*4 (id = unit+0x1DA & 0xFFFF, cap 99999).
evidence: Disassembly of callee 0x00612A94 shows the per-id increment and the 0x0001869F (99999) cap, and the list offsets are the documented battle-work unit table; the inherited 'Field_RefreshActorSlots' name had the wrong subsystem and described no effect.

name: Party_CalcAverageLevel
summary: Returns the average level of the active party members as a float in s0: walks the ring at +0x4260/+0x4264, resolves each member record (0x0035EB98 on node+0x768), skips inactive members (0x0062917C) and divides the summed level (member+0xD8) by the count; 0.0f when nobody is active.
evidence: Disassembly shows the 0.0f initialisation, vcvt of member+0xD8, s16 += level, s17 += 1.0f and the final vdiv s0,s16,s17 - the float return Ghidra dropped. The earlier 'UpdateMemberValues' name was wrong: nothing is stored; the caller BattleScene_SpawnMonstersByProgress uses the average level to scale its spawns.

name: maybe_Ui_CloseScreenOnButton
summary: Per-frame screen tick: func_0066D1C0(core) scans the UiCore's two 8-slot resource tables for a slot whose resource byte +0x78 is 4; when one is found it re-binds the scene-flow slot resources and requests animation 9 (the back/close clip) on the screen's animator. Always returns 1.
evidence: The check is not a direct button query: disassembly of 0x0066D1C0 walks the core's slot tables and tests byte +0x78 == 4, so the 'on button' part is inherited; Ui_SceneFlow_BindSlotResources (0x006260B4) and animation id 9 are the only certain parts.

name: maybe_Ui_Node_SetPackedEntryValue

name: maybe_Ui_TwoPageListWindow_Init
signature: void maybe_Ui_TwoPageListWindow_Init(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

evidence: The caller is the confident Ui_EquipmentWindow_Update (0x00199E30); the same table yields 2 ids here, 4 for page 0 and 5 for page 1, so 'two-page list' still describes the component, but no symbol names the window class itself.

name: Field_SceneObject_ShowOverrideA
summary: Show override of a field scene-object class: calls the base Field_SceneObject_Show(self) and returns self. The readable C file continues into the next function because Ghidra merged a split symbol.
evidence: The function is 24 bytes (doc size) and disassembly 0x002188E0..0x002188F7 is exactly `bl 0x005E78E4; mov r0,r4; pop {r4,lr}`; the next prologue starts at 0x002188F8 (maybe_Actor2D_ResetIfRegistered). The containing table 0x0075BC3C is a field scene-object table (Field_SceneObject_Hide, Actor_ResolveHandleWithTypeCheck), so the base class is the safe prefix. The inherited 'ReleaseSpan' summary described the neighbouring function, not this one.

name: Field_SceneObject_ShowOverrideB
summary: Second copy of the field scene-object show override: calls the base Field_SceneObject_Show(self) and returns self; its readable body was merged with Actor2D_ResetPartsIfIdle (0x00219BCC).
evidence: Same 24-byte body as 0x002188E0 - disassembly 0x00219BB4..0x00219BCB is `bl 0x005E78E4; mov r0,r4; pop {r4,lr}`, and the next prologue (Actor2D_ResetPartsIfIdle) starts at 0x00219BCC; nothing is released or freed here. The vtable table 0x0075BCFC is the same field scene-object family.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishTalkText
summary: End-of-talk step: if the node's talk slot +0x298 is set, it may write 0xFF into the shared state byte at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E+slot, then if that byte is 1 or 4 and node->f_B8 is live it refreshes the talk target through 0x002D1258.
evidence: The byte index resolves to the shared pastword/quest block at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E (FACTS.md), so this is not a scene-object-local flag; the exact owner semantics are still unclear, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishMessageAction
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_FinishMessageAction(void* node, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Variant of the talk-action completion: clears the same shared state byte at work+0x24A98+0x5A4E+id to 0xFF when the node is flagged idle, and when the byte is 1 or 4 it plays the talk animation through virtual +0x84, calls 0x005F7784(node,0x3C,0) and clears node[0xAD].
evidence: Same shared state block and same '1 or 4' test as the sibling 0x0040F680; the body acts (void) and the field scene-object table 0x0076DC40 places it next to the confident Field_SceneObject_Hide, but no caller or string names the action.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ShowAttachedA
summary: Show override: calls the base Field_SceneObject_Show(self) and, when the attached draw object at +0x29C exists, tail-calls its virtual +0x60 (the same show slot used for children).
evidence: Disassembly 0x003DE028..0x003DE053; the twin at 0x003DE054 does the same with Field_SceneObject_Hide (0x005E7A34), and both slots belong to the field scene-object table 0x0076A98C, so the class prefix is the base class rather than the inherited 'Field_Actor'.

name: Field_SceneObject_ShowChildren
summary: Show override that also shows every child: base Field_SceneObject_Show(self), then virtual +0x60 on each node of the child ring at +0x2C8/+0x2CC. Its twin at 0x004B2EBC hides the same set.
evidence: asm 0x004B2E80..0x004B2EB8 is exactly the base show plus the child-ring loop; the named Field_MultiPart_ShowChildren (0x0044E250) uses the same pattern, and the twin hide slot sits directly after this one in table 0x007769CC.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ShowAttachedB
summary: Second copy of the show-with-attached-object slot: base Field_SceneObject_Show(self) and then virtual +0x60 on the attached object at +0x29C; the twin at 0x004D7F48 hides it.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x003DE028 (disassembly 0x004D7F1C..0x004D7F47); the inherited 'UpdateSlotA' verb was wrong - the body only shows, and the hide twin follows immediately.

name: maybe_Field_Object_MultiBaseDeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a multi-base field object: installs the caller's vtable, runs Ui_Object_DtorBody on the three base sub-objects (+0x304, -0x4C, -0x100), restores base vtable 0x00758818, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: No string, caller or vtable names the class 'Gimmick'; what is certain is the multi-base deleting-destructor shape (three base walks, the 0x00758818 restore, Field_Object_DtorBase and the free at 0x0010F6CC), so the name now says only that.

name: Actor2D_DeletingDtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of an Actor2D subclass: installs the vtable plus its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the scene node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The body is the shared scene-object deleting-destructor template and the address sits in the Actor2D block right after the named Actor2D_DeletingDtor (0x0021B85C) and Actor2D_DeletingDtor_Subclass (0x0021B8AC); the inherited 'DtorSpanList' wording described no span list.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtorE
summary: Deleting destructor in the 0x31Axxx actor/sprite-actor block: installs the vtable plus its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the object's embedded base node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Body is the standard template (same 56 bytes as 0x0021BC50 etc.) and the block holds maybe_Field_CreateActorRuntimeState (0x0031A8C0) and Gfx_SpriteActor_SetPosAndScale (0x0031AF44); the inherited 'DestroySubObjectAt24C' was wrong because the +0x24C node is the object's own embedded base, not a sub-object it owns.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_DeletingDtorF
summary: Deleting destructor in the 0x36xxxx sprite-actor block: installs the vtable plus its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the embedded base node at +0x24C and runs Field_Object_DtorBase; Ghidra truncates the listing at a bad instruction, so the final free is not visible here.
evidence: The visible half is the standard destructor template and the block contains Gfx_SpriteActor_InitFromRecord (0x00361AC4) and Gfx_SpriteActor_SetAnim (0x00361CB0); the truncated tail means the deleting half cannot be verified, so maybe_ and 0.45.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a sprite actor: stores the caller-supplied vtable and its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the render node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: Seven callers are sprite-actor/battle-action code (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreatePooled, Battle_ActorAction_UpdateMotion, ...), the named sibling Gfx_SpriteActor_DtorB sits at 0x003BC954, and the vtable comes from r1 - which is why Ghidra shows 'arg2'.

name: maybe_Field_ActorSub_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field-actor sub-object: installs the vtable plus its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the embedded node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.

name: maybe_Field_ActorSub_DeletingDtorB

name: Field_Prop_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field prop: installs the vtable plus its +0x98 secondary, unlinks the render node at +0x24C, runs Field_Object_DtorBase and releases the storage through 0x0010F6CC.

name: Field_Object_DeletingDtorD

name: maybe_Ui_DeactivateAttachedWidget
summary: Hides the attached child widget at owner+4 (Ui_TitleWindow_SetButtonVisible(child, 0)) and clears the child's active byte +0x94. No resource is freed.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ClearQuestStateByte

summary: Scene-object command: forwards the command to the children, then for kind 3 maps index through a u16 lookup and writes 0xFF (unset) into GameWork + 0x24A98 + 0x5A4E + id, i.e. into the shared pastword/quest id block.
evidence: The store address 0x2A4E6 equals work+0x24A98+0x5A4E, the pastword/quest table from FACTS.md; the lookup base comes out of the literal pool as only 0x34A, so that branch may be dead, which is why the name keeps maybe_ and only claims the state byte.

name: maybe_Actor_ResetTrailToCurrentState
summary: Builds a trail sample from the actor (0x00161E00), marks its enable byte +0x23, submits it to the trail object reached through (work+8)->f_48 via Gfx_Trail_ResetSamples, then refreshes the actor's action state.
evidence: Gfx_Trail_ResetSamples (0x0023D518, 0.55) collapses a trail's whole sample history onto the given sample and is called by Actor_Action_Trail_End and FieldParty_ResetMemberModels; nothing in the body is a 'move command', so the name now states what the record is.
